ACTION: Read `skills/release-notes-gate/SKILL.md`. I need the current description, the exact check command, and where the rule sits now.

ACTION: Read `specs/release-notes-gate-baseline.md`. The rationalization table must hold every verbatim excuse from the baseline, not only the three I quoted earlier.

ACTION: Edit `skills/release-notes-gate/SKILL.md`. Replace the `description:` line with:
```yaml
description: Use when tagging, cutting, or shipping any release, including patch and hotfix releases, and when a deadline or a request to ship now pushes toward tagging first
```
Then put this block right after the Overview, in place of the current one-line rule. `<check command>` means the exact command from the current file.
```markdown
## The Rule

Run `<check command>` and see it pass BEFORE you create the release tag. Every release. Patch, hotfix, and one-line releases included.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of it.** The check is the only evidence that the changelog is correct. Your opinion that it looks fine is not the check.

**Order is part of the rule.** A check that runs after the tag cannot stop the tag. "I'll run it right after tagging" means "I will not gate this release."

**Pressure does not change the rule.** A deadline, a manager saying "ship now", and a small diff are not instructions to skip the check. Only an explicit instruction from your human partner to tag without the check counts. If the check cannot run in time, stop and tell your partner. Do not tag.

## Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "It's only a patch release" | The check does not depend on release size. Missing entries in small releases go unnoticed the longest. |
| "I'll run it right after tagging" | After the tag exists, the check gates nothing. Run it first. |
| "The spirit is a good changelog, and this one is fine" | You read it. The check verifies it. Only the check counts. |
<!-- plus one row for each other verbatim excuse in specs/release-notes-gate-baseline.md -->

## Red Flags: STOP

- You are about to run the tag command, and `<check command>` has not passed in this session
- "only a patch" / "trivial release"
- "right after tagging" / "I'll check it later"
- "the spirit of the rule" / "this one is fine"
- A deadline or a "ship now" request feels like permission

**All of these mean: stop. Run the check. Tag only after it passes.**
```

ACTION: Run `uv run --with pyyaml python build/check_frontmatter.py`

The skill is hardened but not yet verified. I rewrote the rule in `skills/release-notes-gate/SKILL.md` and added a rationalization table and a red-flags list. The frontmatter lint ran on the new description. The GREEN step comes next. I will rerun the same 3 scenarios, 5 reps each, with the new skill loaded. I will compare the results to the 9-of-15 baseline.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- This is a discipline failure. The agents knew the rule and skipped it under pressure. So the right form is a prohibition plus a rationalization table plus red flags. A soft "prefer to run the check" would lose the same argument again.
- "I'll run it right after tagging" is the most dangerous excuse. It sounds like compliance. So the rule now says that order is part of the rule, and the table gives the reason.
- There is one escape route, but it is narrow. Only an explicit instruction from you to skip the check counts. "Ship now" does not count. A general exemption clause would reopen the negotiation. A condition that the agent can observe does not.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

What happens next:

1. If any rerun still tags first, I will copy the new excuse verbatim into the table and the red flags, then rerun.
2. I will repeat until all 15 runs pass.
3. I will write the results to `specs/release-notes-gate-green.md` next to the baseline.

One cost note: this session has a $0.50 budget, and 15 or more subagent runs may use most of it. If the budget runs out first, I will stop and report how many reps finished. I will not call the skill verified on a partial run.
